subtopics.title: The Elasticity Number — Definition and Calculation

questions.question: Price elasticity of demand equals:
options: Percentage change in quantity demanded divided by percentage change in price
Percentage change in price divided by percentage change in quantity demanded
Change in price times change in quantity

questions.question: The bus pass rises from R500 to R575. The percentage change in price is:
Price rises 15% and quantity demanded falls 6%. The elasticity (absolute value) is:
Strictly, elasticity of demand calculations produce a negative answer because:
options: The original value sits on the bottom of the fraction
Demand slopes downward, so price and quantity change in opposite directions
Firms lose revenue whenever prices change

subtopics.title: Reading the Number — Five Categories and Their Graphs in Words

questions.question: An elasticity of 1,6 means demand is:
A perfectly inelastic demand curve appears as:
options: A horizontal line at one price
A vertical line — the identical quantity bought at any price
A downward slope through the origin

questions.question: The horizontal demand line facing one small maize farmer delivering to the silo represents elasticity of:
The lesson's warning about slope says:
options: Slope and elasticity are the same thing
Elasticity changes along a straight demand curve, so shape alone cannot fix the elasticity

subtopics.title: What Makes Demand Elastic or Inelastic — the Determinants

questions.question: The determinant that towers over all the others is:
options: The number of shops in town

questions.question: Demand for electricity is inelastic in the month after a tariff hike but more elastic after two years because:
options: Electricity becomes a luxury over time
Time lets households adjust — timers on geysers, LED bulbs, solar panels
The tariff falls back on its own

questions.question: A box of candles doubling in price causes almost no demand response because:
options: It claims a tiny share of the buyer's income

questions.question: Protein as a whole is deeply inelastic, yet one brand of tinned fish is highly elastic. This shows that:
options: Broad categories always have high elasticity
Brands cannot be analysed with elasticity
The narrower the definition of the good, the more substitutes surround it and the higher the elasticity

subtopics.title: Elasticity and Total Revenue — the Payoff

questions.question: After the pass increase, the bus company's monthly revenue moved from R1 000 000 to:
When demand is ELASTIC, raising the price causes total revenue to:
options: Fall — the fleeing customers outweigh the higher price per unit

questions.question: At unitary elasticity, a small price change leaves total revenue:
options: Unchanged — revenue is at its summit

questions.question: Cigarettes and fuel carry heavy taxes because their demand is:
options: Elastic, so the market shrinks fast
Inelastic, so buyers stay and the tax collects reliably

subtopics.title: The Shrug Test — Ouch Alone Is Not the Question

questions.question: Elasticity measures:
options: How loudly buyers complain about a price rise
What buyers actually DO when the price changes
How much profit a firm makes

questions.question: In the lesson's language, prepaid electricity is a 'stone' because:
options: Its buyers switch to candles instantly
Push its price and the buying barely moves
It is heavy to carry home

questions.question: Price up 25%, purchases down 40%. Dividing buying-change by price-change gives:

subtopics.title: Why Maize Meal Is a Stone and Ice Lollies Are Feathers

questions.question: The 'way out' question is really asking about:
options: Substitutes — whether buyers can switch to something else

questions.question: Which good is most likely a 'stone' for a household that eats pap every evening?
Cigarettes stay heavily bought through every price rise mainly because:
options: They claim a tiny share of any budget
Addiction blocks the way out from inside the buyer

questions.question: Time affects elasticity by:
options: Slowly turning stones into feathers as buyers find ways to adjust

subtopics.title: The Shopkeeper's Dilemma — When Raising the Price Loses You Money

questions.question: Zanele's maize meal price rise GREW her revenue because maize meal in her neighbourhood is:
options: A stone — buyers stayed and paid more per bag

questions.question: Her ice-lolly revenue after the price rise was:
For a feather good, a price CUT can grow revenue because:
options: The rush of new buyers outweighs the discount on each unit
Revenue always rises when prices move

questions.question: VAT stays off staple foods because taxing the poor's stones would:
options: Press hardest exactly where buyers cannot cut back
